subject: Storage zones that improve kitchen flow
hook: From flat board to a pan drawer that closes itself: how a cooking zone gets built.
ig:
From flat board to a pan drawer that closes itself: how a cooking zone gets built.

The cooking zone is the busiest part of most kitchens, which is why we usually plan deep pan drawers either side of the hob rather than cupboards. You pull the drawer out and lift the pan straight up, instead of kneeling down and reaching into the back of a dark cupboard.

Here is how one comes together in our workshop:
• Panels cut to suit the exact width of your hob run
• ABS edging applied, so edges wipe clean and resist knocks
• Drilled for runners and fixings on the boring machine
• Assembled and checked on the bench before it leaves

Soft-close is standard, so the drawer finishes its own journey quietly, even fully loaded.

fb:
Ever knelt on the kitchen floor fishing for a lid at the back of a cupboard? That is the problem pan drawers solve.

This is a quick look at how one gets made in our Hanley workshop: cut on the panel saw, edged, drilled for runners, then assembled and checked on the bench. The finished drawer sits next to the hob, so pans, lids and trays lift straight out where you need them. Soft-close comes as standard.

It is one small part of planning a kitchen around the way you actually cook. See more about our bespoke kitchens here:
